generalfeedback.text:
The factors give the intercepts: \(y = 0\) at \(x = {@m0@}\) and \(x = {@n0@}\). The squared factor \({@(x-m0)^2@}\) is never negative, so \(y\) does not change sign at \(x = {@m0@}\): the curve touches the axis there and crosses it at \(x = {@n0@}\).

[[if test="is(a0>0)"]]The leading coefficient is positive, so the curve rises to the right.[[else]]The leading coefficient is negative, so the curve falls to the right.[[/if]]

(a) Graph [[if test="is(pos=1)"]]A[[elif test="is(pos=2)"]]B[[elif test="is(pos=3)"]]C[[else]]D[[/if]]. Graph [[if test="is(pr=1)"]]A[[elif test="is(pr=2)"]]B[[elif test="is(pr=3)"]]C[[else]]D[[/if]] is upside down, Graph [[if test="is(ps=1)"]]A[[elif test="is(ps=2)"]]B[[elif test="is(ps=3)"]]C[[else]]D[[/if]] touches and crosses at the wrong places, and Graph [[if test="is(pm=1)"]]A[[elif test="is(pm=2)"]]B[[elif test="is(pm=3)"]]C[[else]]D[[/if]] is the mirror image in the \(y\)-axis.

(b) \(x = {@m0@}\). (c) \(x = {@n0@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Differentiation II: matching a cubic to its sketch

Grade 12 CBE Core 4.1: Choose the graph of a factorised cubic from four sketches, using the repeated root, the single root and the sign of the leading coefficient.

Core

This question is original to this project.

truefeedback.text: That graph is upside down: the leading coefficient of \(y\) is \({@a0@}\), so \(y\) is large and [[if test="is(a0>0)"]]positive[[else]]negative[[/if]] for large positive \(x\).
That graph touches the \(x\)-axis at \(x = {@n0@}\). The squared factor makes the curve touch the axis at the repeated root.

falsefeedback.text: That graph is the mirror image of the curve in the \(y\)-axis: its intercepts are at the negatives of the right ones.

truefeedback.text: The curve crosses the axis there. It touches where the factor is squared.
